newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Sarajevo bank signs deal with American Express.
newsitem.headline: Sarajevo bank signs deal with American Express.

text.p: Sarajevo's commercial bank "Central banka" signed a general agreement with American Express in December and hopes to issue the first credit cards in March, the bank manager said.
"This is a good sign, both for our bank and for Bosnia. It's a confirmation of economic and political stability," Mehmed Vukotic, the client department manager, told Reuters.
Vukotic said that American Express representatives would be coming to Sarajevo towards the end of the month to work out the final details with the bank.
"We want our citizens to be able to purchase goods with American Express cards issued by a Bosnian bank everywhere in the world," he said.
He said the bank will be a guarantor to American Express for the cards' use.
"We shall have discretion to determine who will be a card holder because we are a guarantor. We will observe our clients' behaviour to determine if the cards are used properly."
The average salary for those in work in Bosnia's Moslem-Croat federation comes to a mere 220 marks.
But merchants have already expressed interest in accepting American Express cards, he said.
"It's in their best interest to sell more and they know we will be behind each card issued," he said.
Central banka, with a 74.4 million-mark capital, was the first bank to start issuing cheques up to the amount of the client's account last September.
